body: I don't see `.eslintignore` mentioned anywhere in the readme. We do have a `.jshintignore` in the repo root, though: https://github.com/eslint/eslint/blob/master/.jshintignore
Sorry should have linked to it, here you go: https://github.com/eslint/eslint/tree/master/docs/command-line-interface

@FredKSchott Are you using grunt to lint (or any other task manager?). Also, where is your .eslintignore file located? If yes - then it is expected behavior, although probably not desired. Currently .eslintignore will only apply if you lint based on directory, if you lint on specific file, it will not apply. Task Managers usually use globs to unwrap a given path and execute command on each file individually.
This was encountered when running from the command line (v0.4.2). .eslintignore exists in the repo top-level directory.
Just reproduced with the command line, as well.

I think (sorry don't have to investigate right now), that the code is looking for .eslintignore from the directory where linting was started from (in your case from `public/`). If the file is in the parent directory, I think it will not be picked up by code. That a compromise, so we wouldn't have to traverse all directories up to the root.

https://github.com/eslint/eslint/blob/master/lib/config.js#L193

eslint caches only last matched pattern in .eslintignore
